# NASHA product bible (generated by tools/blueprint_views.py from canonical data; do not hand-edit)

**Status of every item: DESIGN HYPOTHESIS. Nothing here has been cooked, brewed, tasted, photographed by the founder or reviewed by a professional.** Lane B (digital planning). Evidence stays 4/95 and design 43/95: digital work never raises physical evidence. This page connects each Core 5 food and beer to its cultural references, sensory targets, operations, supply, economics and status from the canonical matrices; fix a fact in the matrix, not here. Concept renders are illustrations, never evidence.

## Core 5 foods

### Chicken 65 Totopos

- **Status:** DESIGNING; Session 1 protocol FROZEN (D-74); physical test: NOT PERFORMED; confidence: medium for the concept; none for any result
- **Cultural references:** Indian anchor: South Indian Chicken 65: small boneless thigh pieces, dry to lightly coated, deep red-orange, curry leaf and green chile (Chennai-associated; origin contested, V-61) Mexican anchor: Fried nixtamal corn totopos as the chip/base (totopos names the chip; NASHA's thick fried chip is a design choice, not a Mexican standard, V-63) Class: MODERN FUSION overall; Chicken 65 = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; thick fried chip = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION; Hyderabad/Andhra lineage = UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR (cultural advisor review NOT done)
- **NASHA transformation:** The chip becomes the plate: chicken and chip are built to be eaten together; crema (not raita) as optional cooling; lime and onion default
- **Core ingredients / construction:** boneless chicken thigh; yogurt-ginger-garlic-lemon marinade; rice flour + cornflour coating; curry leaf; green chile; fried corn tortilla wedges; crema; lime; onion | THREE constructions under test: A Integrated, B Ring, C Composed board (sheet 11); bare-chip control
- **Method and equipment:** Marinate, coat just before frying, fry at about 175 C in small batches, probe to 74 C; chips fried last | fryer (H load), probe thermometer, rack, hot hold 90 C
- **Sensory targets:** Crisp-shell juicy chicken; chip still crisp at T+10 (gate 3.5); heat 3, richness 3, acid 2, char 1, fried 4, fresh 2 (design values 0-5, not measured)
- **Operational constraints:** holding: HIGH: moisture migration into chip; 10-minute failure gate; execution: medium: fryer pressure, second person, oil handling; D-54: low: chicken only; no lard in tortillas or oil; allergens proposed: milk (yogurt, crema); possible egg if cook adds it; wheat NOT expected (rice flour/cornflour) but cross-contact in fryer to be recorded; no allergen-free claim
- **Economic drivers (uncertainty rank 4 of 5, AGENT JUDGEMENT):** chicken thigh; frying oil; nixtamal tortilla chips; crema; curry leaf; fresh chile; supply: MEDIUM: fresh curry leaf specialty; single-source tortilla
- **Cost data:** NONE REAL YET: no receipt has been recorded; `python3 tools/food_costing.py economics` shows every layer NOT COMPUTABLE
- **Pairing:** first flight: mexican-lager (PF-01), pilsner (PF-07); PF-01 mexican-lager (risk hypothesis: low bitterness should not amplify chile; may be too thin for the fat); PF-07 pilsner (risk hypothesis: bitterness plus chile heat) - PAIRING HYPOTHESIS, NOT SENSORY TESTED
- **Plating / vessel direction:** board or plate; crema on the side or integrated per construction; garnish purpose: fried curry leaf and chile = Chicken 65 identity cue; lime/onion = acid and freshness
- **Prototype history:** NO ITERATIONS RECORDED; **photography:** NO FOUNDER PHOTOGRAPHS yet (concept renders exist; illustrative only); **failures:** NONE RECORDED (nothing cooked)
- **Next iteration:** Session 1 exactly as frozen (sheet 13 shopping list and cook card); first economic measurement: Session 1: raw/trimmed/cooked weights, oil in/out, active minutes

### Paneer Tikka Taco

- **Status:** DESIGNING; Session 2 prep (not cooked); physical test: NOT PERFORMED; confidence: medium-low
- **Cultural references:** Indian anchor: Paneer tikka: thick spiced hung-curd marinade, char, soft paneer, onion/capsicum; North Indian/Punjabi restaurant tradition (no documented inventor) Mexican anchor: Corn-tortilla taco with green salsa, raw onion, cilantro, lime; charred-meat-taco (al carbon) is inspiration only and unsourced Class: MODERN FUSION; paneer tikka = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; taco form = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; pineapple = UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR (al pastor echo) (cultural advisor review NOT done)
- **NASHA transformation:** Tandoor-style char on a taco; acid and salsa architecture does what raita/chutney does; optional charred pineapple (never called al pastor)
- **Core ingredients / construction:** paneer (about 2 cm cubes); hung curd, ginger-garlic, chile, kasuri methi, chaat masala, neutral oil (mustard oil EXCLUDED from the baseline, V-72), optional besan/ajwain; corn tortilla 12-15 cm; salsa verde; onion; cilantro; lime | 3-4 cubes per taco (about 45-70 g paneer, TEST START), onion/capsicum 10-15 g, salsa 10-15 g; two small tacos per order
- **Method and equipment:** Marinate 1-4 h; char over very high heat to order (tandoor if available; else charbroiler/comal/oven+broiler as labelled substitute) | tandoor (unresolved) or charbroiler/comal; comal for tortillas
- **Sensory targets:** Soft interior, visible char, crust that clings; tortilla does not tear; heat 2, richness 3, acid 3, char 4, fried 0, fresh 4 (design values 0-5, not measured)
- **Operational constraints:** holding: MEDIUM-HIGH: paneer firms and dries, tortilla steams; finish to order; execution: medium: depends on the unresolved tandoor/hood answer; D-54: low: paneer; check rennet source/animal rennet only matters for vegetarian claims, not D-54; allergens proposed: milk (paneer, yogurt); mustard only if mustard oil or a mustard blend is ever used (excluded from baseline); wheat only if flour tortilla; no allergen-free...
- **Economic drivers (uncertainty rank 2 of 5, AGENT JUDGEMENT):** paneer; tortillas; hung curd and spice; salsa; onion/capsicum; supply: HIGH: paneer sourcing and quality UNKNOWN
- **Cost data:** NONE REAL YET: no receipt has been recorded; `python3 tools/food_costing.py economics` shows every layer NOT COMPUTABLE
- **Pairing:** first flight: witbier (PF-03); PF-03 witbier (risk hypothesis: coriander/citrus clash with lime or yogurt (soapy)) - PAIRING HYPOTHESIS, NOT SENSORY TESTED
- **Plating / vessel direction:** two tacos on a plate, salsa on the side; garnish purpose: salsa and onion supply the Mexican identity and the acid that cuts paneer richness
- **Prototype history:** NO ITERATIONS RECORDED; **photography:** NO FOUNDER PHOTOGRAPHS yet (concept renders exist; illustrative only); **failures:** NONE RECORDED (nothing cooked)
- **Next iteration:** Session 2: ONE variable = heat source; marinade, cut, tortilla constant; hold at 0/5/10 min; first economic measurement: Session 2 heat-source comparison plus a paneer price/spec check

### Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise

- **Status:** DESIGNING; long-lead item; physical test: NOT PERFORMED; confidence: medium-low
- **Cultural references:** Indian anchor: Dum-style sealed-pot braise; whole-spice toasting; bhuna-style frying of the adobo paste (technique only) Mexican anchor: Jalisco birria de chivo: bone-in goat in guajillo-ancho adobo with vinegar and spices, braised, with consomme; corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime, salsa Class: Goat, adobo, consomme, tortilla/onion/cilantro/lime = HISTORICALLY SUPPORTED (T1, advisor to confirm); dipped griddled taco = MODERN FUSION/adaptation (Tijuana/LA, typically beef); sealed pot =... (cultural advisor review NOT done)
- **NASHA transformation:** Keeps goat/adobo/consomme identity; Indian layer limited to technique that improves depth; yogurt-papaya marinade and curry-leaf tadka are TESTED AGAINST a plain adobo control, not assumed
- **Core ingredients / construction:** bone-in goat shoulder/leg; guajillo and ancho adobo (vinegar, Mexican oregano, cumin, cinnamon, clove, bay); goat/chicken/vegetable stock only; corn tortillas; onion; cilantro; lime; salsa | Goat taco(s) with consomme in a small cup; NO cheese by default; bones and visible fibre kept so it reads as goat, not beef
- **Method and equipment:** Sear, bhuna the adobo paste, seal, low braise; skim; dip tortillas in surface fat and griddle | oven or kettle (long braise), comal/griddle, cold storage, hot hold
- **Sensory targets:** Tender but fibrous goat; drinkable consomme; tortilla holds after dipping; heat 2, richness 5, acid 3, char 2, fried 1, fresh 2 (design values 0-5, not measured)
- **Operational constraints:** holding: HIGH: large braise cooling/reheating/hold, fat set in consomme (food-safety professional must set the process); execution: HIGH: long lead, sourcing, yield and trim waste unknown; D-54: MEDIUM: stock and bones must be goat/chicken/vegetable only; no beef stock/bone, no pork lard in tortillas; not halal,...; allergens proposed: milk if yogurt marinade; possible wheat if seal dough; celery/others per stock; no allergen-free claim
- **Economic drivers (uncertainty rank 1 of 5, AGENT JUDGEMENT):** bone-in goat; dried chiles; stock; tortillas; consomme; supply: HIGH: goat supply thin and price volatile (UNKNOWN)
- **Cost data:** NONE REAL YET: no receipt has been recorded; `python3 tools/food_costing.py economics` shows every layer NOT COMPUTABLE
- **Pairing:** first flight: hefeweizen (PF-05), vienna-amber (PF-06); PF-05 hefeweizen (risk hypothesis: clove/banana against clove/cinnamon is a congruence gamble); PF-06 vienna-amber (risk hypothesis: may be heavy with a rich consomme) - PAIRING HYPOTHESIS, NOT SENSORY TESTED
- **Plating / vessel direction:** small clay or steel cup for consomme (katori-like), tacos on a plate; garnish purpose: raw onion, cilantro, lime cut the fat and mark it as Mexican
- **Prototype history:** NO ITERATIONS RECORDED; **photography:** NO FOUNDER PHOTOGRAPHS yet (concept renders exist; illustrative only); **failures:** NONE RECORDED (nothing cooked)
- **Next iteration:** Small pilot per the Session 5 card (about 3 kg bone-in): plain adobo vs adobo+Indian layer (one variable), record yield, trim, skim, 60/120 min hold; blind vs lamb taco; first economic measurement: a single braise with raw/trim/cooked weights and a goat price check

### Gobi Taco

- **Cultural references:** Indian anchor: Gobi 65 (batter-fried, tempered) / tandoori gobi (yogurt-besan roast); Gobi Manchurian is Indo-Chinese and only named if used Mexican anchor: Corn tortilla, lime-cabbage slaw, salsa, pickled onion, cilantro Class: MODERN FUSION / ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION; tamarind-guajillo glaze = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION; no traditional Mexican precedent claimed (cultural advisor review NOT done)

- **Economic drivers (uncertainty rank 5 of 5, AGENT JUDGEMENT):** cauliflower; batter/oven; glaze; slaw; tortilla; supply: MEDIUM: cauliflower price/seasonality
- **Cost data:** NONE REAL YET: no receipt has been recorded; `python3 tools/food_costing.py economics` shows every layer NOT COMPUTABLE
- **Pairing:** first flight: pilsner (PF-02); PF-02 pilsner (risk hypothesis: bitterness beside chile heat may amplify burn) - PAIRING HYPOTHESIS, NOT SENSORY TESTED
- **Plating / vessel direction:** two tacos, salsa on the side; garnish purpose: slaw and pickled onion add acid and crunch; keeps it from reading as fried chicken
- **Prototype history:** NO ITERATIONS RECORDED; **photography:** NO FOUNDER PHOTOGRAPHS yet (concept renders exist; illustrative only); **failures:** NONE RECORDED (nothing cooked)
- **Next iteration:** Write a Gobi Taco test sheet first; primary question fry vs roast; crunch at 0/5/10/15 min; glaze grams vs tortilla softening; first economic measurement: Session with weights and a roast vs fry comparison

### Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla

- **Status:** DESIGNING; Session 4 candidate; physical test: NOT PERFORMED; confidence: medium
- **Cultural references:** Indian anchor: Murgh makhani: tomato-butter-cream gravy, kasuri methi, charred tandoori-style chicken (origin contested in court, do not pick one) Mexican anchor: Quesadilla con rajas: roasted poblano strips, melting cheese (Oaxaca-style), griddled on a comal Class: MODERN FUSION; butter chicken = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; quesadilla con rajas = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; dip = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION (cultural advisor review NOT done)
- **NASHA transformation:** Reduced clingy makhani and charred chicken pieces inside a griddled quesadilla; poblano smoke and acid cut the richness; dip optional and separate
- **Core ingredients / construction:** chicken thigh (about 1 cm dice, tandoori-style char); reduced makhani; roasted poblano rajas (drained); Oaxaca-style cheese (record rennet source); flour or corn tortilla (open) | 25 cm tortilla folded: cheese against both faces as barrier, sauced filling in the centre, rajas against the cheese; TEST START about 40-50 g cheese, 50-70 g chicken-sauce, 20-30 g rajas
- **Method and equipment:** Reduce sauce and chill filling; dry comal, medium heat, light press; rest 1-2 min before cutting | comal/flat-top (H load), tandoor optional for chicken, oven/grill alternative
- **Sensory targets:** Crisp-browned tortilla, set filling, melted cheese fused, no leak; heat 1, richness 5, acid 1, char 2, fried 0, fresh 1 (design values 0-5, not measured)
- **Operational constraints:** holding: MEDIUM: steams soft if covered; filling leaks if sauce not reduced; execution: medium-high: comal is the shared bottleneck; D-54: low (chicken; check tortilla for lard); allergens proposed: milk (butter, cream, cheese, yogurt); wheat if flour tortilla; tree nut only if cashew in the gravy (default cashew-free); no allergen-free claim
- **Economic drivers (uncertainty rank 3 of 5, AGENT JUDGEMENT):** chicken thigh; butter/cream/makhani; poblano; Oaxaca-style cheese; tortilla (corn or flour open); supply: MEDIUM: cheese and tortilla choice open (flour lard risk D-54)
- **Cost data:** NONE REAL YET: no receipt has been recorded; `python3 tools/food_costing.py economics` shows every layer NOT COMPUTABLE
- **Pairing:** first flight: vienna-amber (PF-04), hefeweizen (PF-08); PF-04 vienna-amber (risk hypothesis: Vienna malt may cloy on a sweet cream sauce); PF-08 hefeweizen (risk hypothesis: yeast spice against garam masala) - PAIRING HYPOTHESIS, NOT SENSORY TESTED
- **Plating / vessel direction:** cut wedges showing cross-section; dip in a cup; garnish purpose: rajas and an acid/fresh garnish are the counterweight to richness
- **Prototype history:** NO ITERATIONS RECORDED; **photography:** NO FOUNDER PHOTOGRAPHS yet (concept renders exist; illustrative only); **failures:** NONE RECORDED (nothing cooked)
- **Next iteration:** Session 4: sauce thickness first (spoon-coat/reduction time vs leak minutes); then cheese barrier; then chicken size; first economic measurement: Session with filling weights and comal minutes

## Core 5 beers (BEER PRODUCT DESIGN; no NASHA beer exists and none is brewed)

### NASHA Hefeweizen

- **Status:** GATE BEER; NOT BREWED; physical status: NOT BREWED
- **Style reference / role:** BJCP 10A Weissbier (T1 extract S-107/108); Proof beer: development gate for the claim of a credible integrated program (see 00-BREWER-HANDOFF section 0b); a failure triggers REVISE/DE-PRIORITIZE/REMOVE...
- **Sensory targets (style-typical, not a NASHA result):** colour 2-6 (window 3-5), bitterness 8-15, body medium-light, creamy, yeast POF+ banana/clove; strain decisive, serve 4-7
- **Glass and pairing role:** Collar Weizen about 0.5 L serve (tall vase); carbonation cuts fat; clove echoes warm spice; low bitterness beside heat; first flight: goat-birria (PF-05), butter-chicken-quesadilla (PF-08)
- **Operations / economics (style knowledge; process is the brewer's decision):** tank occupancy SHORT; quality sensitivity MEDIUM (yeast character must be controlled); draft-velocity risk MEDIUM: freshness matters; cloudy beer is not a long-shelf beer (agent...; ingredient complexity LOW-MEDIUM (wheat malt; specific yeast)
- **Questions for a qualified brewer:** yeast strain and temperature/pitch trial design; ferulic rest worth; open vs closed fermentation; turbidity and sediment strategy
- **Regulatory / ingredient issues:** wheat/gluten allergen label; no gluten-free claim; no novelty ingredients; TTB formula status if any adjunct
- **Next step:** Brewer scopes pilot route and yeast trial (pilot-briefs/01)

### NASHA Mexican-Style Lager

- **Status:** GATE BEER; NOT BREWED; physical status: NOT BREWED
- **Style reference / role:** BJCP 2A Pale/International Lager (nearest) and BA Mexican-Style Pale Lager; Session beer for chile-forward food; largest planned volume share
- **Sensory targets (style-typical, not a NASHA result):** colour 2-6 (window 2-4), bitterness BJCP 2A 18-25; BA 15-22; repo window..., body light, fairly dry, yeast clean lager, serve 2-4
- **Glass and pairing role:** Collar Lager about 0.4 L; heat relief; low bitterness does not amplify chile; first flight: chicken-65-totopos (PF-01)
- **Operations / economics (style knowledge; process is the brewer's decision):** tank occupancy LONG; quality sensitivity HIGH (a clean beer has nowhere to hide flaws); draft-velocity risk LOW-MEDIUM: easy-drinking; risk is sameness with Pilsner; ingredient complexity LOW-MEDIUM
- **Questions for a qualified brewer:** does the adjunct earn its place; lager time; water; skunk/light-strike control
- **Regulatory / ingredient issues:** NO lime by default (lime on request only; must not mask faults); TTB formula status if corn adjunct; avoid stereotype framing
- **Next step:** Brewer brief review (pilot-briefs/02); differentiation test vs Pilsner
